newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Group says Taiwan VP Lien also to meet Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Group says Taiwan VP Lien also to meet Dalai Lama.

text.p: Taiwan's number two leader, Vice President and Premier Lien Chan, will meet Tibet's spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, on Wednesday under the auspices of a longtime anti-communist group, sponsors said.

"The two will meet at 7.30 p.m. (1130 GMT) at the Ambassador Hotel," said a spokesman for the World League for Freedom and Democracy, which once included the word "Anti-Communist" in its title. "It is a private dinner hosted by our league president."

Earlier on Wednesday, aides to President Lee Teng-hui gave the first official confirmation of a planned meeting between Lee and the visiting Tibetan Buddhist god-king on Thursday, the end of his unprecedented six-day stay in Nationalist-ruled Taiwan.

The Buddhist monk's meeting with Lee already has angered Beijing, which has assailed it as the collusion of two "splittists" bent on severing both Tibet and Taiwan from the communist Chinese mainland.
The Dalai Lama arrived in Taiwan on Saturday, his first return to Chinese soil since he fled his Himalayan homeland in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Chinese rule.

The Dalai Lama and Taiwan's leaders deny that they seek independence from China. The Tibetan leader has said he wants only self-rule for Tibet, while Lee insists that Beijing first embrace democracy before Taiwan can reunite with the mainland.
